newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T squeezed higher in late trading.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T squeezed higher in late trading.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc were squeezed higher in late trading on Thursday amid a renewed burst of U.S. buying, traders said.
The stock closed up 20p at 486-1/2 in heavy trading of 7 million shares.
Traders said demand for B.A.T shares, partly associated with recent programme trades, had left market-makers short of stock and the price had been pushed higher as a result.
A strong performance in Philip Morris Cos shares on Wall Street, up $1-1/4 at $113-1/8, also helped drive B.A.T higher.

"The whole (London) market is extremely squeezy," said one market-maker, "there were lots of buyers around a few days back who pushed it up to over 490p, and today the buyers have come back... all the buyers are from the U.S."
B.A.T shares have been active in recent sessions amid hopes that the recent underperformance of tobacco stocks overestimated the impact of U.S. lawsuits.
B.A.T has also been boosted by speculation that the company will demerge its tobacco and insurance arms.
Another positive for the stock was today's news of B.A.T's sale of its Henri Wintermans cigar unit.
